title: Tamil Nadu: Rain prompts climbing restrictions at Parvathamalai temple in Tiruvannamalai
excerpt: Tiruvannamalai (Tamil Nadu), Oct 24 (IANS) The Tamil Nadu Forest Department has restricted access to Parvathamalai hill near Kalasapakkam following rains, allowing devotees to begin their climb to the Lord Mallikarjuna Swamy temple only between 5.30 a.m. and 1 p.m. each day. Only people aged between 18 and 60 will be permitted to undertake the trek to the Shiva temple atop the 4,560-foot hill. Children, people with illnesses and persons with disabilities will not be allowed to climb under the restrictions announced by forest officials. Officials said rain had made the steep route slippery, increasing the time needed to negotiate the ascent. Devotees ordinarily require at least four hours to reach the shrine from the foothills, making an early start essential for managing movement along the narrow forest trail. A committee headed by District Collector Vandhana Garg will decide whether visits can be permitted, depending on the rain forecast. Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar, District Forest Officer K. Sudhagar and representatives of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department are members of the committee. Custom Ad: Multiplex The hill falls within the Pudupalayam Range of the Tiruvannamalai Forest Division. Pilgrims approach the temple through a mud pathway near Then Mathimangalam and Then Kadaladi villages, covering approximately 4.5 km through the forest to reach the summit. The pathway is only three feet wide, limiting the space available for devotees making the demanding climb. The temple attracts around 1,000 visitors daily, prompting the department to regulate entry to avoid congestion along the route. Only 100 devotees are allowed to start the ascent every hour as a measure against overcrowding and stampede-like situations. Plastic items and water bottles are banned to prevent littering in the forest. The Parvathamalai area also has more than 30 tribal hamlets, including Kanamalai, Ezhuthampattu, Neepathurai and Arasanoor. An existing mud pathway laid during British rule in the 1920s remains the only connection between these tribal communities and towns in the plains. The restrictions come as officials assess the risks posed by wet terrain on a route used by pilgrims to reach the hilltop shrine. The narrow approach and lengthy ascent make regulating pilgrim movement particularly important during periods of rainfall. Access to the temple will remain subject to the committee’s assessment of weather conditions, alongside the daily timing, age and hourly entry limits imposed by the Forest Department. --IANS aal/uk

title: Karnataka-based Gridflow develops autonomous electric pod transit prototype for dedicated guideways & urban mobility
excerpt: As Indian cities grapple with traffic congestion, rising commute times and growing demand for sustainable mobility, Gridflow Technologies Pvt. Ltd. is developing an alternative to conventional road-based transportation. Gridflow develops autonomous electric pod transit prototype for dedicated guideways The startup has built a prototype of an autonomous electric pod transit system in which compact passenger vehicles travel along dedicated guideways. This allows smooth point-to-point journeys without being affected by regular road traffic. The company's pod is designed to carry up to four passengers or a payload of 400 kg and operate at speeds of around 30 km/h, according to a recent update on the prototype. Gridflow is also planning a demonstration at speeds of up to 60 km/h on a longer guideway, indicating its next steps in testing the system's performance. Founded in 2021, Gridflow Technologies is based in Hubli, Karnataka. Its founder and CEO, Umesh Rudrapatna, is leading the venture's efforts to develop a connected, autonomous, shared and electric transportation infrastructure. The company is building its technology around robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), automation and the Internet of Things (IoT), to create a new layer of urban mobility infrastructure. Dedicated network for autonomous pods The compact electric pods would operate autonomously along these routes, potentially offering passengers direct journeys between designated destinations. The concept is designed to combine the convenience and privacy associated with taxis with the predictability and infrastructure efficiency of public transportation. Gridflow envisions a system in which users can access driverless electric pods much as they would book a ride-hailing service. Rather than following conventional bus routes with multiple stops or relying on private vehicles navigating congested roads, passengers could travel between selected points on a dedicated network. The approach could be particularly relevant for connecting residential areas with workplaces, transit stations and commercial districts. Dedicated guideways may also help address first- and last-mile connectivity gaps around metro and bus networks. By connecting vehicles, guideways and digital control systems, Gridflow aims to make passenger movement more coordinated and efficient. Engineering a new mobility infrastructure Developing such a system involves challenges beyond building an electric pod. The startup must also address guideway engineering, vehicle stability, autonomous navigation, safety, communication systems and the coordination of vehicles operating on a shared network. Gridflow's team brings together expertise in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, robotics and computer science. Its team includes mechanical engineers Mallikarjun V, Omkar G and Vikas H; robotics engineers Vidya N and Yash H; electrical engineer Radhika M; and computer science engineer Vidhatri A, alongside other contributors. The company has also worked on structural engineering concepts for its pod project. An internship project involving isotruss and isogrid structures was undertaken by engineering students under the guidance of Gridflow's management and project mentors, highlighting the role of lightweight structural design in the development process. Gridflow's website says the company is currently developing a minimum viable product (MVP) and seeking proof-of-concept installations with prospective partners. This places the venture in an early development phase, with prototype testing and real-world demonstrations representing important milestones before wider deployment. Targeting sustainability and urban efficiency Gridflow's broader vision is to reduce dependence on private vehicles by making shared transportation more convenient and responsive to passenger needs. The company argues that a dedicated, electrically powered system could reduce congestion, energy consumption and transport-related emissions. The company claims the platform could eventually be adapted for moving goods within industrial facilities, with modular configurations tailored to different payload and space requirements. Gridflow has outlined potential energy savings of 30% compared with electric buses and a 45% reduction in public transportation carbon emissions.

title: Degree is not just for career, but opportunity to contribute to nation-building: Gujarat CM
excerpt: Earning a degree is not merely about building a career but also an opportunity to contribute to nation-building, Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel said on Saturday, addressing the first convocation ceremony of K.N. University at Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar University. Urging graduates to look beyond securing good jobs or establishing businesses, Patel said: "Young people should combine knowledge with humility, success with compassion and strength with responsibility."He emphasised that education should help build character, strengthen the nation and allow people to serve society. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership, the Chief Minister said education had increasingly become a means of empowering young people in the 21st century, extending beyond the pursuit of degrees. Quoting PM Modi, he said: "In university examinations, questions are asked from the syllabus, but in the examination of life, everything is 'out of syllabus'.""While academic progress is measured through grades and marks, success in life depends on continuous hard work and perseverance," he added. Highlighting PM Modi's 25 years of public service, the Chief Minister said the Prime Minister had worked tirelessly for the country and its people. Drawing a lesson from his life, Patel said: "Hard work does not make you tired; rather, the satisfaction of working hard is a reward in itself."Patel expressed confidence that many of the graduates would pursue their own start-ups or business ventures. "Initiatives promoting start-ups, science and skill development had helped create opportunities for young people to become entrepreneurs," he said. Referring to the state's higher education sector, the Chief Minister said education, research and skill development had emerged as key pillars of the state's development under PM Modi's guidance."The emphasis on higher education during PM Modi's tenure as Gujarat Chief Minister had helped private universities, including K.N. University, provide quality education," he said. Around 110 universities are currently operational in Gujarat, according to Patel. He said the National Education Policy placed emphasis on India's knowledge traditions, the mother tongue and modern science."Emerging sectors such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors, robotics, space technology and green energy were opening up new opportunities for graduates to become 'job creators' rather than merely 'job seekers'," he noted. Patel urged young people to play an active role in realising PM Modi's vision of "Viksit Bharat @ 2047".During the ceremony, 22 meritorious students were awarded 22 medals across various disciplines, comprising nine gold, six silver and seven bronze medals. A total of 94 students received degrees in different disciplines.
